version.changelog: Add UTM attribution tags (utm_source=clawhub) to ClawLink branding links so visits from this skill page are tracked as a distinct traffic source.

llm.summary: This Figma skill is coherent and not malicious, but it asks users to install and permanently allow a third-party OAuth plugin with broad access to Figma data and write actions.

dimensions.detail: The ClawLink integration is purpose-aligned but routes OAuth-backed Figma data through a hosted third party and can access sensitive design files, comments, metadata, assets, and webhook data available to the connected account.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install instructions use an unpinned `clawhub:clawlink-plugin`, add it to `tools.alsoAllow`, and restart the gateway; the reviewed artifact does not include the plugin implementation or an immutable version/checksum.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions direct discovery, preview, and confirmation before writes, but enforcement appears to depend on the external ClawLink plugin and agent behavior rather than code in this package.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The setup persistently enables the plugin across future OpenClaw chats and states that ClawLink stores the user's OAuth token; no removal, revocation, retention, or scope details are provided in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's Figma read, export, comment, token, and webhook capabilities match its stated purpose, and write actions are described as requiring confirmation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust ClawLink with the Figma files and actions available to your connected account. Review the plugin source or publisher assurances if available, confirm write actions carefully, and revoke the Figma OAuth connection and remove the plugin when no longer needed.
llm.findings: [T08] unexpected: The Figma integration's use of ClawLink is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but the unpinned privileged plugin plus persistent allowlisting and OAuth token handling create a real review concern because the privileged implementation was not present in the artifact.
